metrics.certificate_note: certificate.kind: none, EXPLICITLY. This contract computes no discrete logarithm and collects no relation, so there is no solve or relation claim to certify (docs/claims-and-verification.md). Its forced-value checks -- the liftable-count identity per curve, T_obs = 0 for `order`, p_lower = 1.0 at R5_PERCLASS, the closed-form-versus-Monte-Carlo null mean, the Hurwitz-Kronecker census -- are internal consistency checks, not certificates, and are reported as such.
metrics.scope: Tier TOY. Instrument characterisation only. No ECDLP claim, no cost or exponent claim, sota_delta zero.
metrics.supersedes_reason: RUN-INSTR-85b102-poolA carries two defective DIAGNOSTIC computations (its measured statistics, p-values and control counts are unaffected and are reproduced bit-for-bit here): (1) residual_in_mc_standard_errors was computed at degenerate rungs where the realized null is a bitwise point mass, so a one-ulp difference was divided by one-ulp-over-sqrt(B) and reported as 100 standard errors of disagreement where the agreement is in fact to the last bit; (2) the exactly-1.0 p-value categoriser recognised only T_obs == 0.0 as a forced boundary value and mislabelled every T_obs lying outside the realized null support as unexplained. implementation_error in reporting. Run records are immutable, so the defective run is preserved and superseded, never overwritten.

tail_checks.check: no p-value exactly 0.0 or 1.0 outside a degenerate rung
tail_checks.note: The contract's stated rationale is that the estimator makes 0.0 impossible, so an observed 0.0 is an implementation defect. Both readings are reported without choosing between them: the LITERAL outcome, and a breakdown separating a tail p-value of exactly 1.0 that is FORCED because T_obs lies at or outside that end of the realized null support (the opposite tail then sits at the resolution floor) from any unexplained case. No p-value of exactly 0.0 is possible under the frozen estimator and none was observed. This check is not one of the contract's stopping rules.

tail_checks.check: closed-form null mean within 3 MC standard errors of the empirical mean for `order` and `full_liftable` at every rung
tail_checks.note: Reported in both readings, choosing neither. At a DEGENERATE rung the within-block label permutation is the identity, so every null draw is bitwise T_obs and the realized null is a point mass; np.mean's pairwise summation of B identical doubles then reports a mean one ulp off, giving a 'Monte-Carlo standard error' of one-ulp-over-sqrt(B). Dividing a one-ulp difference by that produces a large dimensionless number from an exact agreement -- the absolute and relative residual columns show the agreement is at the last bit. Cells with a genuinely non-degenerate null are listed separately and are the ones that could indicate a real disagreement.
